title: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management: what does it detect, who sees it and what does it cost?
summary: The licensing, permissions, commands and control destinations are supported by Microsoft documentation. Corrections should narrow the claim that disabling auditing removes all signals, flag preview agent monitoring, and clarify shortened paths and conflicting Microsoft guidance.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management scores user activity against configured policies.
claims.quote: By using templates, you can select specific risk indicators and customize event thresholds for policy indicators, effectively customizing risk scores, and level and frequency of alerts.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management detects, investigates and acts on malicious and inadvertent internal activity.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management is a compliance solution that helps minimize internal risks by enabling you to detect, investigate, and act on malicious and inadvertent activities in your organization.

claims.claim: Activity matching policy conditions raises alerts for review.
claims.quote: Risk indicators automatically generate alerts when they match policy conditions.

claims.claim: Policies use Microsoft 365 logs.
claims.quote: By using logs from Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Graph, Insider Risk Management enables you to define specific policies to identify risk indicators.

claims.claim: Nothing alerts until a policy is configured.

claims.fix: Replace 'nothing alerts until a policy is configured' with 'the Get started page requires a policy before alerts can trigger. For agents, Microsoft documents a Risky Agents (preview) policy that is automatically present and ready to generate alerts when the service is set up.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/insider-risk-management-monitoring-agents. This distinguishes manual policy creation from the automatically configured agent policy.

claims.claim: Insider Risk Management, Insider Risk Management Admins or Microsoft 365 Global admin can enable analytics.
claims.quote: To enable insider risk analytics, you must be a member of the Insider Risk Management, Insider Risk Management Admins, or Microsoft 365 Global admin role group.

claims.claim: Role membership is edited through Settings > Roles and groups > Roles groups > Insider Risk Management > Edit > Choose users.
claims.quote:
Select Settings in the upper-right corner of the page, select Roles and groups, then select Roles groups in the left navigation pane.
3. Select the Insider Risk Management role group, then select Edit.
4. Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "Insider Risk Management" -Member <user> adds a role-group member.
claims.quote:
Add-RoleGroupMember
    [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter>
    -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter>

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember is available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Applicable: Exchange Server 2010, Exchange Server 2013, Exchange Server 2016, Exchange Server 2019, Exchange Server SE, Exchange Online, Security & Compliance, Built-in security add-on for on-premises mailboxes

claims.claim: Auditing can be enabled through Audit > Start recording user and admin activity in the Purview portal.
claims.quote: Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables Microsoft 365 auditing.
claims.quote:
Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing.

    Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Enabling or disabling auditing requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The auditing toggle command must run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Complete the following steps to turn on auditing by using Exchange Online PowerShell:

claims.claim: The Start recording user and admin activity banner appears only when auditing is off.
claims.quote: If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.

claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled in Exchange Online PowerShell verifies auditing status.
claims.quote:
To verify that auditing is turned on for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell:

Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled

claims.claim: The Status column on Policies displays policy warnings.
claims.quote: The Status column on the Policies tab alerts you to policy issues that might prevent user activity from being reported or explain why the number of activity alerts is unusual.

claims.where: What to check: users in scope
claims.claim: The Users in scope column on Policies shows the included-user count for a policy.
claims.quote: The Users in scope column on the Policies tab shows the number of included users for a policy.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; What to check: Global exclusions
claims.claim: Global exclusions can exclude file types from risk scoring by all Insider Risk Management policies.
claims.quote: You can exclude specific file types from all Insider Risk Management policy matching. For example, you might want to exclude all .wav files. Files with that extension are ignored for risk scoring by all Insider Risk Management policies.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; What to check: Global exclusions
claims.claim: Global exclusions can make policies ignore activities involving specified keywords.
claims.quote: Your Insider Risk Management policies ignore activities related to files or email subjects containing the keyword and don't generate alerts.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; What to check: Global exclusions
claims.claim: Global exclusions can suppress policy alerts for activities in specified file paths.
claims.quote: When you exclude file paths, user activities that map to specific indicators and that occur in those file path locations don't generate policy alerts.
